claims.text: CrCoNi is a compositionally complex medium-entropy alloy.
The CrCoNi alloy is single phase.
CrCoNi exhibits a ductile–brittle–ductile transition as a function of temperature.
CrCoNi has excellent overall resistance to temper embrittlement.
CrCoNi undergoes a temporary reduction in ductility in an intermediate temperature range.
The temporary reduction in ductility is caused by changes in dislocation mobility and subtle alterations of the grain-boundary state.
The homogenized CrCoNi alloy has a stable microstructure before testing.
Grain-boundary structures and dislocation configurations in CrCoNi adjust with temperature.
Localized short-range ordering may be temporarily activated in the intermediate temperature window.
Limited grain-boundary segregation may occur in the intermediate temperature window.
At low temperatures, high dislocation activation energy and the alloy's inherent toughness maintain ductility.
A change in the dominant slip systems at intermediate temperatures reduces ductility.
Transient grain-boundary effects at intermediate temperatures may reduce ductility.
At higher temperatures, increased atomic mobility helps restore ductile behavior.
The absence of conventional segregative temper embrittlement at higher temperatures helps restore ductile behavior.
Ductility is high at both low and high testing temperatures and drops sharply within a narrow intermediate-temperature window.
CrCoNi is known to be ductile outside the proposed intermediate-temperature window.
Changes in composition, processing history, or strain rate may alter the temperature range or magnitude of the transition.
The lack of conventional temper embrittlement in compositionally complex alloys is well evidenced.
